title: A Ember for the Oath
premise: Cyrus Eriksen, a cartographer who maps realms that shouldn't exist for a guild trading in impossible things, inherits a dying stranger's map — and with it the stranger's memories, which bleed into his own each time he draws. The map leads to King Aldric, bound body and soul to the usurper Veyra's crown, an artifact that feeds on oaths sworn in good faith. As Veyra's armies march on the free cities, Cyrus must gather the scattered witnesses of Aldric's original coronation oath, learning that survival has always been paid for with someone else's memory. In the end, Cyrus unbinds Aldric by offering his own inherited memories as ransom — losing the stranger, and part of himself — while the free cities hold, and the guild's ledgers record a debt no one can collect.
about_author: Orsen Nystrom is a former harbor surveyor from the northern coast who claims he began writing fiction after misplacing an entire fjord on a nautical chart. He lives quietly with two opinionated cats and a growing collection of antique maps he refuses to have appraised.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. In the guildhall of the Cartographers' Compact, Cyrus balances ledgers of traded impossibilities — bottled rivers, borrowed years — while hiding that he can read maps no one else can. A dying stranger collapses at his door, pressing a bloodstained chart into his hands and whispering 'the crown remembers.' Emotional beat: reluctant duty, the first crack in Cyrus's safe, ordered life.

chapters.title: Ink That Isn't His
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. The map redraws itself nightly, and Cyrus begins dreaming in a dead man's voice — memories of a coronation oath betrayed. Guild archivist Maren recognizes the hand as royal cartographer Sef Holm, missing for nine years. When guild assassins come for the chart, Cyrus flees with it rather than surrender it. Emotional beat: fear curdling into complicity; he is now part of the story.

chapters.title: Roads the Guild Never Drew
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus, with interludes from Maren. On the road east toward the capital, the map opens paths through unmapped realms — a forest that rearranges itself around regret. Cyrus meets Tessa, a deserter from Veyra's army who confirms the king still lives, hollow-eyed behind the crown. Emotional beat: wary alliance; Cyrus realizes the map is choosing its route, not him.

chapters.title: What the Crown Eats
chapters.summary: POV: Tessa. Tessa recounts what she saw at court: the crown feeding on oaths, leaving the king a vessel and Veyra ever-younger. She reveals Sef Holm was her father's friend, and that the dying stranger's memories now live in Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief and guilt — Tessa deserted instead of fighting, and sees in Cyrus a chance at absolution.

chapters.title: The Witnesses of the Oath
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Following the map's memory-traces, they find three surviving witnesses of Aldric's coronation: a blind priestess, a disgraced knight, and a child now old. Each holds a fragment of the original oath — but reciting them costs the speaker cherished memories. One witness pays willingly; another refuses. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — every step forward is bought with someone's past.

chapters.title: Veyra's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV: Veyra. The usurper senses her crown straining against distant counter-oaths. Flashbacks reveal she took the throne to save the realm from a plague of forgetting — and believes only total control of memory can prevent its return. Her armies burn archives as they advance. Emotional beat: chilling sympathy; Veyra is not wrong about the danger, only about the cure.

chapters.title: The City That Sold Its Name
chapters.summary: POV: Maren. The free city of Halveth bargains with Veyra's envoys, offering to surrender its founding-oath for mercy. Maren arrives undercover to steal the oath-fragment before the trade, and finds the guild has already sold out Cyrus. Betrayed by her own order, she defects with the fragment and a warning. Emotional beat: disillusionment turned to resolve; institutions fail, people don't have to.

chapters.title: Throne of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Cyrus reaches the capital through the map's last unmapped road and stands before King Aldric — who begs him, lucid for one breath, to end it even if it kills him. Veyra captures the group; the crown begins draining Cyrus's inherited memories, forcing him to relive Sef Holm's death. Emotional beat: despair at the nadir — the plan requires a price Cyrus isn't sure he can pay.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. At the climax, the witnesses' fragments are spoken aloud as Veyra's armies breach the walls. Cyrus offers the full weight of Sef's memories — and his own name in the guild ledgers — as ransom, unbinding Aldric from the crown. Veyra, stripped of her stolen years, chooses to stand against the plague of forgetting one last time rather than flee. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into release; the cost is real and permanent.

chapters.title: A Map With Room to Draw
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus, coda from Maren. Weeks later, Aldric rules a battered but free confederation of cities, and the crown lies inert — remembering nothing. Cyrus, missing pieces of himself and all of Sef Holm, takes up blank parchment instead of inherited charts, mapping forward rather than backward. Maren founds a new compact where debts can be forgiven. Emotional beat: quiet hope — inheritance means choosing what to carry.
